purpose: Independent hosted direct comparison of automatic source-format down-holds
scope: Direct WebRTC inside an isolated Docker bridge. No tunnel, TURN, edge authentication, MediaMTX or physical camera is exercised.
Each down-hold runs on a separate hosted Linux runner and has separately built image digests. The ladder and workload differ only by downHold; this is not a same-host/same-image crossover.

All three one-second trials pass unchanged gates. All three three-second trials fail playback and viewer recovery because freeze counters increase after the four-second transition accounting window. All six format and source-target recovery gates pass.
Total initial freeze duration overlaps between groups. These trials alone do not establish a uniform freeze-duration reduction, a startup effect or a reason to change public defaults.

Frame-gap timing uses retained browser expected-display timestamps and the host-recorded shaping phase start without extra clock calibration. It is diagnostic, not a replacement for the unchanged sampled-counter gates; the third three-second gap ends near the phase boundary.
CPU summaries average entire phases, including format transitions. They do not establish embedded-device consumption. Pixel latency measurement is disabled.
Every completed trial and failed verdict is retained. Public downHold remains three seconds pending the same-runner comparison.
